votes.outcome: passed by roll call; five ayes heard (Allison, Leighton, Gray, Blatt, Stolen Bruni) plus the chair

budget_items.topic: Debt capacity and Turkey Hill needs
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said debt capacity is limited and Turkey Hill's near-term system costs must be known so enough capacity is left. No final numbers exist for the hybrid.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities funding for capital items
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said grant money is available for heating, ventilation, windows and envelope work, and urged capital planning to coordinate with the green group.
The committee did not submit an ARPA or capital planning request. It expects another ARPA opportunity in January and must decide what funds it needs through annual town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Cost of a standalone gym or metal structure
budget_items.what_was_said: The School Committee suggested a low-cost metal gym structure; members guessed a regulation gym would be very costly and a tent might be cheaper. No cost was established.

budget_items.topic: Town Hall renovation and code compliance cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The APDC rep warned that converting Town Hall to meeting space will cost money for code compliance, such as fire-rated stairwells and sprinklers.

decisions.decision: January meetings set for Wednesday the 4th and Thursday the 12th, 6 to 7 pm, replacing the holiday dates.
Next meeting will include a vote on whether to pursue and improve the hybrid concept.
Chair will note exploring use of the City United gym as a follow-up item.
Chair will email the town manager and the capital planning chair about available green-funding money.
Chair and two members plan to attend the Planning Board on the 9th.
Outstanding prior minutes to be approved at the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The committee heard Select Board, School Committee and APDC feedback on the Ritter, Town Hall and TC Passios scenarios, which generally favored the hybrid concept.
The School Committee's letter raised homes for the Early Learning Center, Community Link and extended day, plus gym space and Turkey Hill upkeep.
No votes were taken except adjournment; the committee plans to vote at its next meeting on whether to pursue and improve the hybrid concept.
The committee submitted no ARPA or capital planning request and expects another ARPA opportunity in January.
January meetings were set for the 4th and 12th, 6 to 7 pm, replacing the holiday dates.

why_it_matters: The hybrid concept is moving toward a committee vote, and its cost, debt capacity and Turkey Hill system needs are not yet established, so any later request for town funds rests on numbers that do not exist yet.
Converting Town Hall to meeting space would bring code-compliance costs, and the school-space needs raised here could add to what the town budget, mostly taxes, is asked to carry.
watch_next: The committee's vote on whether to pursue and improve the hybrid concept at the next meeting.
January meetings on Wednesday the 4th and Thursday the 12th, 6 to 7 pm, and the January ARPA opportunity.
